questions.q: In the lab, why is `PrepAngle` written as a `function` rather than an `operation`?
options: Because functions run faster on hardware than operations
Because it only computes a fixed classical value (PI()/3.0) with no qubit involvement or side effects, matching the pure/deterministic contract a function requires
Because `Ry` cannot be called from inside an operation
Because PrepAngle needs to call Adjoint
questions.explain: PrepAngle does nothing but return a deterministic classical Double -- exactly the contract a function is meant to express, and exactly why it can't touch a qubit.

questions.q: What verified probabilities does `PrepareState` (Ry(PI()/3) applied to |0>) produce on measurement?
questions.explain: Hand-multiplying the Ry(60-degree) matrix against |0> gives amplitudes [cos(30deg), sin(30deg)] = [0.866..., 0.5], and squaring gives P(0) = 0.75 and P(1) = 0.25 exactly.

questions.q: After `PrepareState(q)` followed by `Adjoint PrepareState(q)` in `PrepareThenUndo`, what does `M(q)` return?
options: Zero with probability 0.75, One with probability 0.25, same as the original preparation
A random mix, since Adjoint only approximates the inverse
Zero with certainty (probability 1.0), because Ry(-theta) composed with Ry(theta) is exactly the identity
One with certainty, because Adjoint flips the final state
questions.explain: The compiler-generated Adjoint of Ry(theta) is Ry(-theta). Multiplying Ry(-theta) by Ry(theta) gives the identity matrix exactly, so the qubit returns to |0> with no residual amplitude on |1> -- verified by direct matrix multiplication.

questions.q: In `ConditionalPrep`, what happens to `target` if `ctrl` is left in the |0> state (never flipped with X)?
options: target is forced into |1>
target is unaffected by the Controlled call and stays |0>, so M(target) returns Zero with certainty
target receives the full Ry(PI()/3) rotation regardless of ctrl's state
The program fails to compile because ctrl must always be |1>
questions.explain: Controlled PrepareState([ctrl], target) only applies PrepareState's effect when ctrl is |1>. With ctrl left at |0>, the controlled operation acts as identity on target, which remains |0>.

questions.q: Why does the lab insist on computing the Ry matrix multiplication by hand rather than just stating the probabilities?
options: Because Q#'s documentation doesn't specify what Ry does

Because stating a specific numeric probability without independently verifying it risks asserting an invented or incorrect number -- the lab's claims are checked against actual matrix arithmetic instead
Because the simulator cannot compute Ry probabilities itself
Because hand computation is required syntax in Q# programs
questions.explain: Any specific numeric claim (like P(0) = 0.75) needs to be independently verified by real computation rather than assumed or guessed -- the lab works through the matrix-vector multiplication explicitly for exactly this reason.
